sentences.text: This second bail application has been filed by applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of bail in connection with Crime No.143 of 2023 registered at Police Station Kotwali, Ashok Nagar, District Ashok Nagar (M.P.) for offence punishable under Sections 363, 366-A, 376(2)(n), 506, 370(A), 376, 120-B, 34 of IPC and Sections 5, 9 of POCSO Act.
Applicant was arrested on 13-05-2023.

First bail application of applicant was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 9th of November,
2023 passed by this Court in MCRC No.46299 of 2023.
Thereafter, statements of father and mother of victim have been recorded on 07th of December, 2023 before the Trial Court.

sentences.text: As per the case of prosecution, father of the victim reported to PS Kotwali, Ashok Nagar on 10-03-2023 that his daughter is missing since morning.
Some unknown person has allured and taken his daughter.
PS Kotwali, Ashok Nagar registered FIR in Crime No.143 of 2023 for offence punishable under Section 363 of IPC.
During search, the victim was recovered on 13-05-2023 from the house of accused Mukesh at Village Sirlai, PS Bhikan Gaon, District Khargone.

In her statements recorded under Sections 161 and 164 of CrPC, the victim alleged that accused Dharmendra had allured her and taken to the house of Mukesh (applicant) and sold her for an amount of Rs.1,20,000/-.
Mukesh committed rape on her on the pretext of marrying with her.
She got pregnant.
She revealed to Mukesh that Dharmendra is not related to her and she left her home without informing her parents.
Thereafter, Mukesh contacted her parents.
The police recovered her from the house of Mukesh from Village Sirlai.
On such allegations, prosecution for offence under Sections 366-A, 376(2)(n), 506, 370(A), 376, 120-B, 34 of IPC and Sections 5, 9 of POCSO Act was added.
Applicant was arrested on 13-05-2023 and he is in custody ever since.
On completion of investigation, Final Report was submitted on 18-07-2023.
The trial is underway.
Learned Counsel for the applicant, in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application, submits that applicant has been falsely implicated in this matter.
The applicant is aged about 26 years and he is labourer by profession.
Dharmendra impersonating himself as uncle of victim, got him married with the victim without stating correct facts.
He himself has informed the parents of the victim.
Learned Counsel further submits that no criminal antecedent is reported against applicant.
The statements of victim and her parents have been recorded before the trial Court.
Victim (PW1), her father (PW2) and mother (PW3) did not support the prosecution.
Further, all of them have specifically stated that at the time of alleged incident, the victim was aged about more than eighteen years.
There is no likelihhod of his tampering with the remaining evidence.

Indar Khede and Bhuriya Bai have been extended the benefit of bail by this Court vide orders dated 19th of September, 2023 and 1st of June, 2023 passed by this Court in MCRC No. 36681 of 2023 and 23465 of 2023.
Jail incarceration is causing great hardship of applicant and his family.
Trial would take time to conclude.
Therefore, the applicant may be extended the benefit of bail.
Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/State opposes the bail application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence.
Learned Counsel submits that DNA report suggests involvement of applicant in the alleged offence.
In reply, learned Counsel for the applicant submits that the victim has denied all the allegations against the applicant.
Further, she was major at the time of incident.
Therefore, no offence is made out against the applicant.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
Considering the arguments advanced by both the parties and overall circumstances of the case, but without commenting on merits of the case, this Court is inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Thus, the application is allowed.
